checks.declared: A provider byte reading reaches the card unmodified: no rescaling, no refill, no default.
The aggregate total equals the sum of the readings it included, never an independent estimate.
Bytes a local scan measured enter the distribution total at their measured value.
A local scan never produces a remote-scope record; the constructor refuses it instead of relabelling it.
checks.observed: localScan reported as remote is refused

checks.declared: A reading stamped after the injected clock cannot be live data; it is refused rather than reported as fresh.
All shipped seams classify one future stamp the same way, so two surfaces cannot disagree about what is live.
A reading older than the stale window is marked stale, not fresh.

A provider-reported binary unit is converted to bytes before the total is folded, and the raw reading itself keeps the value the provider reported; the account is never silently excluded from its own total.
checks.observed: mega raw 3/20 (gibibytes); aggregate used=3221226472 quota=21474838480 available=18253612008 included=[mega, dropbox] excluded=[]

checks.declared: A provider-defined unit stays excluded and visible instead of being guessed at.
A value below a unit boundary keeps that unit: it may be rounded inside the unit, but never up to the next one, where `1000 KB` would read as the 1 MB it is not.
checks.observed: raw 999999 B rendered as "999.99 KB" = 999990 B, unit ceiling 1000000 B

checks.declared: One card renders used/available/quota through one unit rule, so a reader can reconcile the numbers printed on it.
checks.observed: card: "100% used, 1 B available of 1 MB"

checks.declared: A user-declared value keeps its own source label and makes the total non-exact; it never reports as measured data.
The distribution report declares reference mock values unusable in production and performs no provider read itself.
With no readable provider reading the aggregate reports unavailable with null totals, never zero bytes.
A provider that omits its quota reads "Quota unavailable" on every surface, never a zero-byte quota.
